result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both pages have heavy bold type, a strikethrough on the cancelled row and status pills with a word in them. A's statuses are easier to read in bright sun because they use black text on saturated yellow and add icons (!, ×, ✓), while B's brown-on-peach and green-on-pale-green pills are lower contrast. B's times line up better because every hour has two digits, whereas A's mix of 8:00 and 10:00 is left-aligned and doesn't line up. In both screenshots the phone number is cut off below the fold, and the font stack can't be checked from an image beyond seeing that both use a single system-style sans, so items 4 and 5 are scored provisionally at 3. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B is easier to read in bright sun: its text is darker and heavier, and each status has an icon (!, ✕, ✓) as well as a bold word in a badge, so it doesn't rely on colour alone. However, B left-aligns times with one- and two-digit hours, so the colons in 8:00 and 10:00 don't line up. A's times all have two-digit hours, so its columns scan cleanly. Neither screenshot shows the phone number or the font stack, so those items get neutral scores for both.
